summary: Implemented GET /api/v1/settings/audit-log (TENANT_ADMIN only, paged) on top of the foundation task's tenant_audit_log model (app/models/tracker.py::TenantAuditLog, migration CreateTenantAuditLog): app/schemas/settings_audit_log.py (AuditLogEntryResponse, AuditLogListResponse, AuditLogQueryParams), app/repositories/settings_audit_log.py (tenant-scoped, date-range/user/action-type filtered, newest-first query), app/services/settings_audit_log.py (read-only mapping to the response DTO -- no write path exists for this resource at all), app/routers/settings_audit_log.py, wired into app/main.py. The endpoint is read-only by construction: there is no PUT/PATCH/DELETE route for audit-log entries, so UC11-BR-005/BR-011/AF-006's 'cannot be edited or deleted' requirement is enforced by routing itself (no handler exists to invoke) rather than a runtime check. Added tests/test_settings_audit_log.py covering the role matrix (401/403), empty list, newest-first ordering, Filter Date Range filtering, userFilter/actionTypeFilter filtering, tenant scoping, and that no write route exists for the resource. Verified behaviorally: no live Postgres is reachable in this sandbox (consistent with prior tasks in this run), so used an in-process FastAPI TestClient against the real app with a sqlite-backed session -- 401 (missing X-User-Role), 403 (APPROVER role rejected), 200 happy path with every response field name/casing/nesting matching the contract (id, logDateTime, logUser, logAction, logEntity, details), 200 with actionTypeFilter applied, 400 on a malformed query param (page=not-a-number) returning the shared {error, details} body, and app.openapi() confirming the route appears under its exact path with the UserRoleHeader/UserIdHeader security schemes declared. `python -m compileall app` passed and `pytest -q` passed (325 passed, including this task's 8 new tests).

pr.title: Implement settings/audit-log endpoint (UC11 Audit Log Tab)
pr.body: Adds GET /api/v1/settings/audit-log for TENANT_ADMIN: schemas, repository, service and router, plus tests covering the role matrix, filtering, newest-first ordering, tenant scoping, and the read-only nature of the resource. Builds on the tenant_audit_log model/migration already added by the foundation task.

blockers: context.json names only the single-entry `AuditLogEntryResponse` DTO, but the endpoint is marked `is_paged: true`. Per CLAUDE.md's paging convention and this module's own pattern for its other paged-but-wrapper-less contract entries (e.g. the approval-rules list), added `AuditLogListResponse` (items/page/pageSize/totalCount) as the actual response body -- an added DTO, not a renamed or invented field, recorded here per TASK.md's 'a missing field' guidance.

This task's table list says 'none -- created by the foundation task', but the `tenant_audit_log` table is actually defined and migrated under the lifecycle-uc10-uc11 module's own context.json/skill (migration CreateTenantAuditLog, model TenantAuditLog in app/models/tracker.py), not a separate T-00-FOUNDATION-API task. Treated it as the pre-existing table this task is scoped to read, per CLAUDE.md's 'import and extend what exists' rule -- no new table or migration was added.

The stories (UC11-AF-002, AF-004, AF-007, BR-003, BR-004, BR-006, BR-013 through BR-017) describe many *write-side* behaviors elsewhere in the Settings/Admin screen (user creation, deactivation, approval-rule creation, integration connect/disconnect, notification updates) that are each expected to append an audit-log entry as a side effect. This task owns only the read endpoint (GET /api/v1/settings/audit-log) per its endpoint table -- it does not implement those other resources' write paths or their audit-append side effects, since those belong to their own tasks (e.g. T-SETTINGS-APPROVAL-RULES-API, T-SETTINGS-USERS-API, T-SETTINGS-INTEGRATIONS-API, T-SETTINGS-NOTIFICATIONS-API). This endpoint will correctly surface whatever entries those tasks' services insert into tenant_audit_log, but no audit-log-writing code was added here.

UC11-BR-005/BR-011/AF-006's 'audit log entries cannot be edited or deleted' requirement is implemented by never exposing a PUT/PATCH/DELETE route for this resource (so such a request 404s/405s at the routing layer) rather than a runtime 'blocked' error with the literal message 'Audit log entries cannot be modified or deleted' -- context.json defines no such write endpoint for this task to attach that message to, and inventing one would violate the 'never invent an endpoint' rule. Tested that no write route exists instead.

TASK.md's verification steps reference `dotnet build`/`dotnet test`/`dotnet run`, which contradict this repo's actual Python/FastAPI stack per CLAUDE.md and the existing codebase -- ran `python -m compileall app`, `pytest -q`, and an in-process FastAPI boot (TestClient) instead, per CLAUDE.md's authority on HOW to build.

No live Postgres instance is reachable in this sandbox, so the curl-against-a-booted-uvicorn-server step in TASK.md's verification list was instead performed via an in-process FastAPI TestClient against the real app with a sqlite-backed session, matching the substitution already used by every other task in this run (see tests/conftest.py and prior tasks' recorded blockers).
